title: Superacids
description: Acids a million million times stronger than sulfuric - strong enough to protonate almost anything.

puzzle.goal: A weakly basic indicator B is dissolved in a superacid and partly protonated to BH⁺. The acidity is measured by how far the protonation goes. Write the acidity function from the standard free energy of deprotonation of BH⁺ (converted to a base-10 logarithm) plus the log of the ratio of unprotonated to protonated indicator.
puzzle.name: Hammett acidity function
puzzle.form: Δ * G / ( R * T * ln ( 10 ) ) + log ( c _ B / c _ BH )
puzzle.expr: dG / ( R * T * ln ( 10 ) ) + ln ( cB / cBH ) / ln ( 10 )
puzzle.ask: Find H0 for an indicator whose deprotonation free energy is given, when it is @{cBH} times more protonated than not.
puzzle.method: Write the acid dissociation constant of BH⁺ as a Boltzmann factor of its free energy, take minus its base-10 log, and add the log of the base-to-acid ratio.
